entries.title: At least 132 killed in Colombia's largest earthquake in years
entries.snippet: The magnitude 7.4 quake had its epicentre in Chocó province, near the Pacific Coast, but could be felt in cities hundreds of kilometres away.

entries.title: Canada flight cancelled after child refuses to wear seat belt
entries.snippet: The incident has sparked a debate over child safety and discipline on commercial planes.

entries.title: At least 13 killed in Ukrainian drone strike deep into Russia
entries.snippet: Russian officials say another 75 people were injured by the attack - one of the deadliest Ukrainian drone attacks since Moscow's full-scale invasion.

entries.title: Netanyahu's rejection of Trump's 15-point Gaza plan unlikely to be final word
entries.snippet: The Trump administration is said to be unbothered by the Israeli prime minister's rejection of the deal, viewing it as campaign rhetoric ahead of a general election.

entries.title: 'We've had a lot of close calls': Canada wildfire evacuees wonder if they still have homes
entries.snippet: More than 12,000 people have been forced to evacuate and some homes have been lost after a wildfire tore through Canada's picturesque Okanagan region.

entries.title: 30 years later, a former gang member will stand trial for Tupac's murder
entries.snippet: It’s been three decades since Tupac was killed, and since then, his reputation has only grown.

entries.title: We are chasing Ebola virus - it is ahead of us, WHO warns
entries.snippet: Infection rates are high, adding to concern that authorities are struggling to get to grips with the disease.

entries.title: Trump signs order to limit childhood vaccines and split MMR shots
entries.snippet: The American Academy of Pediatrics calls the recommendation on measles, mumps and rubella shots "dangerous".

entries.title: World's oceans hit record-high July temperatures
entries.snippet: Global oceans recorded their hottest July on record, partly fuelled by developing El Niño conditions, as wildfires continue to ravage western Europe.

entries.title: New train service connects Finland and Sweden for first time in decades
entries.snippet: The service will enable rail travel from Portugal to Lapland - what is believed to be the longest train journey in Europe.

entries.title: Russian court bars only anti-war party from standing in parliamentary elections
entries.snippet: Russia's only liberal, anti-war party will not be able to take part in next month's parliamentary elections, a Moscow court rules.

entries.title: Nvidia gets $500bn from major investors to develop AI infrastructure
entries.snippet: The money will be used to develop new data centres to house, operate, and cool miles of stacked computer chips that process AI data and actions.

entries.title: The transgender controversy surrounding the WNBA
entries.snippet: After the Indiana Fever's Sophie Cunningham said it was "common sense" to ban transgender women from women's sports, a row has emerged in the WNBA - with former NBA players saying eligibility rules mean they can enter the 2027 Draft.

entries.title: The lonely Chinese men being conned by fake brides
entries.snippet: "Flash marriage" scams are an extreme symptom of a demographic crisis long in the making in China.

entries.title: Hundreds arrested over French wildfires, but who is to blame?
entries.snippet: The government is trying to attribute blame for the unprecedented fires which tore through the country last month.

entries.title: Australia is the planet's extinction hotspot, but one animal offers a glimmer of hope
entries.snippet: The country is home to some of the world's most unique species - but it is losing them at an alarming rate.

entries.title: Watch: Moment powerful earthquake shakes Colombia and crumbles buildings
entries.snippet: At least 111 people have been killed and dozens more injured after the 7.4 temblor hit the western part of the country, according to local officials.

entries.title: Watch: What we know about suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan
entries.snippet: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan, one of the world's most wanted men, has spent his first night in custody in Ireland after being extradited from Dubai.

entries.title: Young girl finds whale stranded on Australian beach
entries.snippet: The humpback whale later successfully freed itself after the tide rose in Queensland, Australia.

entries.title: How Kinahan's hearing unfolded inside the courtroom in Dublin
entries.snippet: Suspected crime boss Daniel Kinahan appeared in court and was charged with directing the activities of a criminal organisation after being extradited from Dubai.

entries.title: Alabama heads into a second primary election after redistricting
entries.snippet: Alabama voters are again selecting candidates for four Congressional districts after the state changed the district map to favor Republicans. The redistricting is causing confusion among voters.

entries.title: After his Reflecting Pool vandalism case is dismissed, David Hearn looks for closure
entries.snippet: The ex-Olympian accused of damaging the reflecting pool tells NPR the experience has been "Orwellian" and "Kafkaesque." And it's not over yet: His lawyers are fighting to close the case permanently.

entries.title: Trump and RFK Jr. try again to upend vaccines for kids
entries.snippet: President Trump signed an executive order on Monday about vaccines, saying children should get fewer. His administration has been blocked in the courts from changing the vaccine schedule.

entries.title: 'The Nerd Reich' tracks the 'unmasking of Silicon Valley's true politics'
entries.snippet: Journalist Gil Durán argues that a small circle of Silicon Valley billionaires and venture capitalists have concluded that democracy is in their way — and that they should be governing in its place.

entries.title: Despite Mideast wars, 20 million gather in Iraq for Shia pilgrimage
entries.snippet: Despite wars ranging across the Middle East, more than 20 million Shia pilgrims gather in Iraq shrine city for Arbaeen festival

entries.title: Does spending money make you feel bad? Read this comic
entries.snippet: If spending — or not spending — money makes you feel shame or regret, you might be grappling with financial guilt. Financial planner Lauryn Williams breaks down three types and how to deal.

entries.title: Flood death toll in India's Assam reaches 100 as thousands lose their homes
entries.snippet: Days of heavy monsoon rain has caused rivers, including the Brahmaputra, to overflow, inundating communities, disrupting livelihoods and damaging infrastructure.

entries.title: Decades of abuse revealed at Michigan art school. And, the Iran war's impact on midterms
entries.snippet: A new report has revealed decades of alleged abuse at an elite art school. NPR spoke with one of the victims. And, Iran is playing the long game with negotiations, which could impact midterms.

entries.title: People with disabilities say Medicaid income limits can stifle career advancement
entries.snippet: Medicaid will have new work requirements next year. But some people with disabilities, who already work, say they'd like to work more, but risk losing their Medicaid coverage if they earn too much.

entries.title: In a competitive Maine Senate race, women voters could be the deciders
entries.snippet: The race between Susan Collins and Troy Jackson is one of this year's most high-profile Senate contests. To win, both candidates will need support from an especially powerful voting bloc: Maine women.

entries.title: Taylor Farms recalls several jalapeño products over salmonella concerns
entries.snippet: Guacamole, pico de gallo and taco dip are some of the prepared foods included in the recall. The announcement comes a few weeks after Taylor Farms voluntarily recalled its iceberg lettuce products sourced from central Mexico because of a potential link to a multistate cyclospora

entries.title: Contiguous U.S. broke its record for hottest month ever in July, NOAA says
entries.snippet: Although it was unusually cool in Alaska, hotter-than-normal conditions blanketed the Lower 48, with the most excessive heat in the Mountain West, Southwest, Northern Plains and Southeast.

entries.title: What we know about the death of Tasia Fortune in Mississippi
entries.snippet: The hanging death of Tasia Fortune, whose body was found outside an abandoned house, has shaken her family and community in Mississippi, where two other people have been found hanging from trees in less than a year.

entries.title: 7.4-magnitude earthquake rocks Colombia, crumbling homes and buildings
entries.snippet: A powerful and deadly earthquake hit Colombia on Monday, killing at least 111 people, toppling buildings and leaving a trail of destruction. Geoff Bennett reports.

entries.snippet: Iran doubled down on keeping the Strait of Hormuz closed until the U.S. meets a sweeping list of demands. President Trump scoffed at those conditions, especially paying reparations to Iran for damages caused by five months of U.S.-Israeli bombardments. The impasse comes as war ap

entries.title: What Meta's new open-source AI model means for the future of artificial intelligence
entries.snippet: Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, has released a free artificial intelligence tool. The release was accompanied by a 14-page essay from CEO Mark Zuckerberg championing his view of how AI could transform our world and what protections are required. William Brangham

entries.title: Family of Marine veteran imprisoned in Russia warns he's near death
entries.snippet: The family of a U.S. Marine veteran imprisoned in Russia says his health is deteriorating and he may be on the brink of death. Robert Gilman was arrested in Russia in 2022 for allegedly hitting a Russian police officer. He was sentenced to four and a half years in prison, but tha

entries.title: Danube's critically low level reveals relics from the past
entries.snippet: In Europe, a climate crisis is unearthing history. Months of brutal heat waves have left the Danube River at a critically low level. But as the water vanishes, it's revealing remarkable relics from the past, including Nazi warships and even the fossilized bones of a woolly mammot

entries.title: This Medicare Part D subsidy is expiring. We answered your questions
entries.snippet: The Trump administration's move to discontinue the subsidy is raising concerns among Medicare Part D enrollees about how much they'll pay for coverage.

entries.title: How pop culture and social media are changing how people talk
entries.snippet: Judy Woodruff has been speaking to a host of experts about the country's 250th anniversary for her "In Pursuit of Happiness" podcast. That includes conversations about the roles satire, national parks and music have played in our history. The latest episode looks at how American

entries.title: Todd Blanche sworn in as attorney general after bruising confirmation battle
entries.snippet: With the confirmation fight behind him, Blanche now faces the challenge of having to navigate the demands of a president who has made no secret his desire to use the law enforcement agency to target his political foes.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump signs executive order on childhood vaccine recommendations
entries.snippet: The order recommends separating the MMR vaccine into three different shots administered in separate visits, and directs the nation's health department to improve vaccine research, says a White House fact sheet.

entries.title: Congo's fast-moving Ebola outbreak started month before it was declared, WHO says
entries.snippet: The World Health Organization says the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak started in February, months before it was officially declared in May.

entries.title: Ukraine's drone chief says push to cripple Russia in Crimea is just getting started
entries.snippet: Ukraine's drone forces could strike seven times more targets in Crimea if Western funding came faster, according to the commander leading Ukraine's drone war.

entries.title: Ukrainian drone attack on oil hub deep inside Russia kills 13, official says
entries.snippet: Authorities in Russia's Tatarstan region say a Ukrainian drone strike on the petroleum hub of Nizhnekamsk killed 13 people and wounded 78 others in one of the deadliest attacks of the 4-year-old war.

entries.title: NOAA says contiguous U.S. set record in July for hottest month ever
entries.snippet: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration says the contiguous United States set a record for its hottest month ever in July.

entries.title: Thousands evacuated as wildfires burn across western U.S. and Canada
entries.snippet: Wildfires are burning across the western U.S. and Canada, leaving some residents keeping a wary eye out for possible evacuation orders.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Turkey MPs back historic law on reintegrating PKK militants
entries.snippet: Turkey's parliament has taken a major step toward ending four decades of conflict with the PKK. The new law sets out how some militants can return to civilian life, but leaves Abdullah Ocalan's future unresolved.

entries.title: Russia: Top court bans opposition anti-war party from vote
entries.snippet: Yabloko, Russia's only anti-war party, has been barred from September's parliamentary elections. The motion to bar Yabloko was filed by the nationalist pro-Kremlin party Rodina.

entries.title: Colombia earthquake: Death toll rises to over 100
entries.snippet: A powerful earthquake, measured at magnitude 7.4, has struck Colombia, killing dozens of people and trapping many under rubble. Cities including Cali, Pereira and Manizales were among the hardest-hit.

entries.title: Why the Rhine drought is bad news for Germany's recovery
entries.snippet: Germany’s inland waterways still move around 5% of the nation's goods. With the Rhine at a critically low level, DW explores how the drought is hitting the economy where it hurts most.

entries.title: India news: Jharkhand police use tear gas, water cannons to disperse student protesters
entries.snippet: Police used force to disperse students marching towards the Jharkhand assembly, as protests over alleged irregularities in government recruitment exams entered their third week. DW has more.

entries.title: Which country is the new Mecca defense pact targeting?
entries.snippet: Observers suggest the new alliance between Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan won't result in any of the countries fighting for each other. Instead it's about preventing Iran and Israel from regional dominance, they say.

entries.title: How climate change is reshaping Africa's malaria risk
entries.snippet: Researchers say warming temperatures are altering malaria transmission patterns across Africa, creating new challenges for health systems and disease control.

entries.title: Middle East: Iran wants US concessions before opening Hormuz
entries.snippet: Iran's Foreign Ministry reiterated that the US must meet Tehran's demands before the Strait of Hormuz is reopened. Meanwhile, Germany says Trump's plan for Gaza could get Hamas to put down its weapons. DW has more.

entries.title: ASEAN closing ranks as cyberscam threat escalates
entries.snippet: Southeast Asian governments are searching for a joint strategy against cyberscammers, a criminal industry that has grown too big, too connected and too embedded in ASEAN economies to be solved just by policing.

entries.title: India: Anger over exam irregularities spreads to Jharkhand
entries.snippet: Inspired by the Cockroach movement, young people in India's eastern state of Jharkhand are marching on the state assembly to demand transparency and a probe into alleged irregularities in civil service recruitment exams.

entries.title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino
entries.snippet: A few weeks ago, Gianni Infantino looked set for another unopposed term as FIFA president. Now, with an election looming, the beleagured football executive is counting the numbers and could be hanging by a thread.

entries.title: Ukrainian drone attack kills at least 13 in central Russia
entries.snippet: Ukraine launched hundreds of drones at targets inside Russia, according to Russian officials. The strikes killed more than a dozen in one of Kyiv's deadliest attacks since the Russian invasion began over four years ago.

entries.title: Thai ex-lawmaker shoots local official dead over loan
entries.snippet: A former lawmaker confessed to shooting a senior official at a government office over a money dispute, police have said. The incident came just days after Thailand's deadliest shooting in nearly four years.

entries.title: When extreme heat threatens Europe's nuclear power
entries.snippet: Warm rivers and low water levels are forcing nuclear power plants to reduce output across Europe. Over a year, the losses are minimal, but on critical days the loss of power has consequences for grids and prices.

entries.title: China: Typhoon Dolphin prompts mass evacuation, canceled flights
entries.snippet: Even as it weakens, Typhoon Dolphin is disrupting life in China. Close to 1,500 flights have been canceled in Shanghai while parts of Beijing are under flood alert.

entries.title: Germany news: Low water on Rhine could sever freight route
entries.snippet: Germany's inland shipping association has warned that the Rhine could soon become effectively split in two as water levels continue to fall. In Berlin, a man was shot dead near a busy central transport hub. DW has more.

entries.title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
entries.snippet: British researchers say rates of type 2 diabetes are growing most among women under 40. The disease is often underdiagnosed in women or diagnosed too late to reverse the condition's progression.

entries.title: Is Iran's middle class being pushed into poverty?
entries.snippet: The war has intensified Iran's economic crisis, squeezing household budgets, hurting businesses and raising fears that millions of middle-income families are slipping closer to poverty.

entries.title: Western Europe records hottest June and July on record
entries.snippet: Drought is gripping large parts of Europe, with soils unusually dry and major rivers running low. A strengthening El Nino could push global temperatures even higher later this year.
